label: Python
plain: A widely used programming language for back-end services, data work and automation.

label: Java
plain: A programming language common in large company systems, banking and Android apps.

label: Kotlin
plain: A modern language mainly used for Android apps and some back-end services; close relative of Java.

label: JavaScript
plain: The language that makes websites interactive; also used on servers (Node.js).

label: TypeScript
plain: JavaScript with extra checks that catch mistakes early; standard in larger web projects.

label: C#
plain: Microsoft's main programming language, used for business software, games (Unity) and cloud services.

label: C / C++
plain: Low-level languages for software that must be fast or run on devices: machines, cars, telecom gear.

label: Go
plain: A language from Google for fast, simple network and cloud services.

label: Rust
plain: A newer language for fast and safe system software; growing in embedded and infrastructure work.

label: SQL / databases
plain: The standard way to store, search and combine data in databases.

label: React
plain: The most common toolkit for building the screens of web applications.

label: UX / UI design
plain: Designing how a product looks and how easy it is to use, based on research with real users.

esco.title: create prototype of user experience solutions

label: Figma
plain: The standard design tool for drawing app and website screens and prototypes.

label: User research
plain: Interviewing and observing users to find out what they need and where they struggle.

label: AWS (Amazon cloud)
plain: Amazon's cloud: renting servers and services over the internet instead of owning machines.

label: Azure (Microsoft cloud)
plain: Microsoft's cloud platform; common in companies that already use Microsoft products.

label: Docker / containers
plain: Packaging software so it runs the same way on any computer or server.

label: Kubernetes
plain: A system that runs and scales many containers (packaged programs) across many servers automatically.

label: CI/CD pipelines
plain: Automation that tests and releases new software versions safely, many times a day.

label: Linux administration
plain: Running and maintaining the operating system most servers use.

label: Infrastructure as code
plain: Describing servers and networks in text files so they can be created and changed reliably.

label: Machine learning
plain: Building models that learn patterns from data, e.g. to predict demand or recognise images.

label: Data pipelines
plain: Moving and cleaning large amounts of data so analysts and models can use it.

esco.title: data extraction, transformation and loading tools

label: Data analysis / BI
plain: Turning data into reports and dashboards that help people decide (e.g. Power BI, Tableau).

label: Statistics
plain: Mathematical methods to tell real effects from chance in data.

label: LLM / generative AI apps
plain: Building products on top of AI language models like ChatGPT: prompts, retrieval, evaluation.

label: Test automation
plain: Writing programs that check software automatically, so errors are caught before users see them.

label: Manual testing
plain: Systematically trying software by hand to find errors and document them.

label: Embedded software
plain: Software inside physical devices (machines, sensors, vehicles) with tight limits on memory and power.

label: Electronics design
plain: Designing circuit boards and the hardware that embedded software runs on.

label: Robotics / ROS
plain: Programming robots to sense and move; ROS is a common robot software toolkit.

label: Cybersecurity
plain: Protecting systems and data from attacks: finding weaknesses, monitoring, responding to incidents.

label: Networking
plain: Configuring how computers and devices connect and talk to each other.

label: Identity & access management
plain: Controlling who may log in and what each person may access.

label: Agile / Scrum
plain: A way of working in short cycles with frequent feedback; most software teams use it.

label: Project management
plain: Planning work, schedules and budgets and keeping a team on track.

label: Product management
plain: Deciding what a product should do next, based on customers and business goals.

label: IT support
plain: Helping users with computers, accounts and software problems.

label: SAP / ERP systems
plain: Large business software for finance, purchasing and logistics; needs specialist configuration.

esco.title: manage standard enterprise resource planning system

label: CRM systems
plain: Software for managing customer relationships and sales (e.g. Salesforce, HubSpot).

label: Mobile apps (iOS/Android)
plain: Building apps for phones.

label: Game development / Unity
plain: Building games or 3D interactive apps, often with the Unity or Unreal engines.

label: Telecom / 5G
plain: The technology behind mobile networks, a big industry in Espoo.

label: GIS / map data
plain: Working with map and location data.

label: Health-data regulation
plain: Rules for medical software and patient data (e.g. MDR, GDPR in health).
